did_you_know.text: The phrase "beyond the Jordan to the west" reflects an ancient directional viewpoint — 'beyond the Jordan' from the writer's perspective.
"Swords of flint" most likely refers to cutting tools made of flint; flint knives appear in archaeological finds as ancient cutting tools and weapons.
The number "forty years" often functions in the Bible as a marker for a generation, which explains why those born in the wilderness had not yet received circumcision until entering the land.
The name Gilgal is related to the root 'to roll'; tradition interprets it as marking the 'rolling away' of Egypt's reproach, and holding Passover there symbolizes a new beginning in the land.
The title "commander of the LORD's host" is a subject of traditional debate: some read it as a warrior-angel, others interpret it as a theophany (an appearance of God).
